title: Who Makes the Decision? Auditing an Agentic LLM Pipeline for Illicit Cryptocurrency Transaction Monitoring
author: Vaishnavi Chaughule, Yuchen Zhang, Mohammed Ahnaf Tajwar, Sai Akshay Menta et al.

summary: Agentic pipelines that combine graph detectors, deterministic rules, retrieval-augmented generation and an LLM judge are being proposed to monitor illicit cryptocurrency flows and to write regulation-citing justifications for analysts. They are evaluated on end-to-end accuracy or on the quality of those justifications, and neither shows which component made a decision.
takeaways: They are evaluated on end-to-end accuracy or on the quality of those justifications, and neither shows which component made a decision.

We audit such a pipeline on the Elliptic++ Bitcoin dataset with decision-source attribution, a trace-level protocol with three layers: per-case actual causation, interventional Shapley credit, and mediation of upstream risk scores.
For illicit-activity monitoring, an LLM's justification should therefore not be read as evidence of which component flagged a transaction.
